name: War Profiteering
window: At the start of a space combat, if both players' flagships are in the active system
text: Choose 1 of those players. If that player wins the space combat, gain 4 trade goods.
flavorText: Gurno Aggero never cared which fleet burned. He only cared that the right one was still flying when the smoke cleared.
automationNotes: Offered in the space combat card list. Pick a player with ships in the active system; you may back yourself or the neutral player. If no system is active, pick the combat system first. If your pick is the only one with ships left after hits are assigned, you gain 4 trade goods. Check the both-flagships condition yourself. Wins by retreat are not detected and the bet ends with the turn. If both fleets die, the bot may pay out before the last hits are assigned; correct that by hand.

name: Extended Campaigning
text: Choose 1 player who is not your neighbor. You may resolve a transaction with that player; if they accept it, they may ready their agent.
flavorText: Xxekir Grom spent a decade touring worlds that had never heard a Xxcha speak. Every one of them remembered his gifts.
automationNotes: Lists players you are not neighbors with and lets you transact with them this turn (also opens fog comms). Once the target accepts a transaction with you this turn, they get buttons to ready an agent.

name: Trade Ships
window: At the start of your turn
text: Choose 1 other player. You and that player may resolve a transaction this turn as if you were neighbors.
flavorText: The convoy flew Hacan colors, carried Winnu escorts, and bore a manifest no one cared to read too closely.
automationNotes: Pick the player; you may transact with them this turn as if neighbors (also opens fog comms). Play it at the start of your turn yourself.

name: Final Stand
window: At the start of a round of ground combat
text: For the rest of ground combat on a planet you control, if you have exactly 1 infantry on a planet and no other ground forces, you roll additional dice equal to the planet's influence.
flavorText: The last Letnev trooper on the ridge primed every charge she had left, and waited for the Sol marines to learn how expensive one soldier could be.
automationNotes: Pick the planet of the ground combat. While you have exactly 1 infantry and no other ground forces there, the extra dice are added to your normal ground combat rolls.

name: Public Reprimand
window: After another player gains trade goods from an action card
text: That player must either spend 3 influence or lose all of their trade goods.
flavorText: Before the full Council, Xxekir Grom read the ledger aloud, line by line, until the Mentak envoy remembered somewhere urgent to be.
automationNotes: Pick the player; they choose to pay 3 influence (with the payment buttons; the amount is not checked) or lose all of their trade goods. Play it at the right moment yourself.

name: Compound Interest
text: Place this card and up to 4 of your trade goods in your play area. At the start of the next strategy phase, remove this card and gain twice as many trade goods as are on it.
flavorText: The Quinarra trading houses have a saying: a trade good spent is gone, but a trade good lent is merely waiting to multiply.

name: Preservation Act
window: When a player you are not neighbors with purges 1 or more relic fragments
text: Gain up to 2 of the relic fragments being purged instead.
flavorText: The Jol-Nar archivists filed a formal protest, then quietly dispatched a retrieval team before the fragments could be lost forever.
automationNotes: Players who are not neighbors of a player purging fragments get a play prompt; you then gain up to 2 of the purged fragments. The purging player's own effect still resolves. Only purges made with the explore fragment buttons are seen; /relic purge_fragments and other purges need a manual fix.

name: Divisive Plot
window: When you win a ground combat against a player who has an unplayed strategy card
text: You may perform the secondary ability of that strategy card, using a strategy token from your reinforcements.
flavorText: While the defenders counted their dead, Yssaril agents were already reading the orders on their war council's table.
automationNotes: Pick the player and their unplayed strategy card. If you have a command token in your reinforcements, you get that card's secondary buttons and your strategy pool is not touched; with none, the card has no effect. Check the ground combat win yourself. Homebrew strategy cards without secondary buttons are resolved by hand.

name: Conflagration
window: After another player gains control of a planet you control
text: Destroy all but 1 of that player's infantry on that planet.
flavorText: "Leave them nothing but ash," Adjudicator Ba'al ordered, and the last shuttles lifted off through a wall of flame.

name: Conflagration
window: After another player gains control of a planet you control
text: Destroy all but 1 of that player's infantry on that planet.
flavorText: The invaders took the capital by nightfall. By dawn, the fuel depots beneath their new barracks had done the rest.

name: Denounce Leadership
text: Purge 1 Support for the Throne in your play area. Then, draw 1 secret objective.
flavorText: Taivra stood before the Galactic Council and named his patron a fraud. By morning, three delegations had torn up their pledges.

name: Embassy Rider
text: You cannot vote on this agenda. Predict aloud an outcome of this agenda. If your prediction is correct, draw 1 secret objective.
flavorText: The Xxcha embassy on Mecatol Rex abstained from the vote. It did not abstain from the wagers placed in its corridors.

name: Dummy Rider
text: You cannot vote on this agenda. Predict aloud an outcome of this agenda. If your prediction is correct, draw 1 action card. If it is not, return this card to your hand.
notes: If Hide Within the Fine Print or Objection Gambit follows this card and that prediction is wrong, that card also returns to its player's hand.
flavorText: No one in the Council chamber could say who had filed the motion. Ssruu, watching from the rafters, said nothing at all.

name: Public Outcry
text: You cannot vote on this agenda. Predict aloud an outcome of this agenda. Players cannot vote against your prediction without placing 1 command token from their reinforcements in a system that contains 1 or more of their non-fighter ships.
notes: Hide Within the Fine Print and Objection Gambit cannot follow this card.
flavorText: Crowds filled the plazas of Mecatol City, and every delegate who crossed them was reminded whose name the people were chanting.
automationNotes: The prediction is recorded and you are skipped when voting. The rule that others cannot vote against it without placing a command token is not enforced.

name: Hide Within the Fine Print
window: After a player plays a Rider other than Politics Rider on the "For" or "Against" outcome of an agenda
text: You may also follow the text of that Rider as if you had played it on the same outcome.
notes: Cannot follow Public Outcry. If this card follows a Dummy Rider and that prediction is wrong, this card returns to your hand.
flavorText: Clause 4,112, subsection nine: "any party may append its interests hereto." The Hacan lawyers had written it centuries ago, and waited patiently.
automationNotes: Offered when a Rider lands on For or Against; you follow a chosen Rider on the same outcome and the bot pays it out like that Rider. Riders the bot does not pay out are resolved by hand.

name: Objection Gambit
window: After a player plays a Rider other than Politics Rider on the "For" or "Against" outcome of an agenda
text: You may also follow the text of that Rider as if you had played it on the opposing outcome.
notes: Cannot follow Public Outcry. If this card follows a Dummy Rider and that prediction is wrong, this card returns to your hand.
flavorText: "Objection," the Naalu delegate said softly. Z'eu only smiled; she had foreseen both answers.
automationNotes: Offered when a Rider lands on For or Against; you follow a chosen Rider on the opposing outcome and the bot pays it out like that Rider. Riders the bot does not pay out are resolved by hand.

name: Siphon Funds
text: Choose 2 players whose home systems are more than 5 hexes away from yours. You may take 1 commodity or 1 trade good from each of them.
notes: You may take from fewer than 2 players, or from none. Commodities you take become trade goods. Picking something a player does not have does not use up that player.
flavorText: The Hacan ledgers always balanced perfectly, no matter how many small sums went missing along the far trade lanes.

name: Siphon Funds
text: Choose 2 players whose home systems are more than 5 hexes away from yours. You may take 1 commodity or 1 trade good from each of them.
notes: You may take from fewer than 2 players, or from none. Commodities you take become trade goods. Picking something a player does not have does not use up that player.
flavorText: Somewhere between the third and fourth relay station, a tithe became a toll, and the toll became a habit.

name: Siphon Funds
text: Choose 2 players whose home systems are more than 5 hexes away from yours. You may take 1 commodity or 1 trade good from each of them.
notes: You may take from fewer than 2 players, or from none. Commodities you take become trade goods. Picking something a player does not have does not use up that player.
flavorText: The Mentak called it salvage rights. Their victims called it theft. The auditors called it lunch.

name: Siphon Funds
text: Choose 2 players whose home systems are more than 5 hexes away from yours. You may take 1 commodity or 1 trade good from each of them.
notes: You may take from fewer than 2 players, or from none. Commodities you take become trade goods. Picking something a player does not have does not use up that player.
flavorText: No single transfer was large enough to notice. That was the whole point.

name: Price of Information
text: Choose 1 player you are not neighbors with whose home system is more than 5 hexes away from yours. That player may show you 1 of their unscored secret objectives; if they do, they gain 2 commodities.
flavorText: The Yssaril broker named a modest price. The Letnev envoy paid it, and only later wondered which of them had learned more.

name: Price of Information
text: Choose 1 player you are not neighbors with whose home system is more than 5 hexes away from yours. That player may show you 1 of their unscored secret objectives; if they do, they gain 2 commodities.
flavorText: "Everyone has a secret," the Naalu oracle whispered. "Most will part with it for the right gift."

name: And Then They Blew Up!
text: Choose 1 system that is more than 5 hexes away from your home system. Destroy up to 2 fighters in that system.
flavorText: The Mentak gunners swore it was a routine calibration test. The debris field took three days to clear.

name: Folding of Spacetime
text: Target a system on the edge of the game board. Each player with ships in this system may move these ships to any other system on the edge of the game board not containing another player's ships.
flavorText: The Creuss call it a shortcut. Everyone who has ever been dragged through one calls it something else.
automationNotes: Players with ships in the chosen edge system get destination buttons and move all of their ships and other units in space. Moving only some ships is manual.

name: Antidisestablishmentarianism
window: When a player's structure on a planet more than 5 hexes away from your home system is destroyed
text: Replenish your commodities. The player who lost the structure may also replenish their commodities.
flavorText: No one on the Council could pronounce the Winnu reconstruction act, but every delegate voted to fund it.
automationNotes: Offered when a PDS or space dock is destroyed on a planet more than 5 hexes from your home; replenishes you and offers the other player a replenish. Only the latest destruction can be answered, until the next strategy phase. Structures removed without being destroyed are not detected.

name: Distant Maps
text: Choose 1 planet more than 5 hexes away from your home system. Reveal the top card of the exploration deck that matches that planet's trait. The player who controls that planet may give you 2 trade goods to explore it.
notes: On a planet with more than one trait, you choose which exploration deck to reveal.
flavorText: The Empyrean charts showed worlds no Council delegate had ever visited, and, for a price, the way there.
automationNotes: Uncontrolled planets and your own planets are not offered.

name: Distant Maps
text: Choose 1 planet more than 5 hexes away from your home system. Reveal the top card of the exploration deck that matches that planet's trait. The player who controls that planet may give you 2 trade goods to explore it.
notes: On a planet with more than one trait, you choose which exploration deck to reveal.
flavorText: Old Lazax cartographers left their charts unfinished. The blank spaces sold for more than the rest.
automationNotes: Uncontrolled planets and your own planets are not offered.

name: Unverified Forgeries
text: Choose 1 player whose home system is more than 5 hexes away from yours. That player may spend 2 trade goods. If they are able to and do not, you may take up to 2 of their relic fragments.
flavorText: The Jol-Nar appraiser declared the fragment authentic. The Yin forger who had made it was quietly relieved.

name: Subjective Justice
window: After a player whose home system is more than 5 hexes away from yours casts votes during the agenda phase
text: Cast 5 additional votes for the outcome that player voted for.
notes: You cast these 5 votes yourself, in the same window as that player's vote.
flavorText: Justice, the Xxcha say, is a matter of perspective. From far enough away, any verdict looks fair.
automationNotes: Pick a far-away player who has already voted; 5 votes are added to their outcome as your votes. Play it right after they vote yourself.

name: Subjective Justice
window: After a player whose home system is more than 5 hexes away from yours casts votes during the agenda phase
text: Cast 5 additional votes for the outcome that player voted for.
notes: You cast these 5 votes yourself, in the same window as that player's vote.
flavorText: The Winnu magistrate ruled from a world so distant that the verdict arrived after the war it settled.
automationNotes: Pick a far-away player who has already voted; 5 votes are added to their outcome as your votes. Play it right after they vote yourself.

name: Extreme Renewal
text: Choose 1 other player. That player may remove all of their units from the game board and all units from their home system, then place their starting units in their home system. If they do, they draw 2 action cards and replenish their commodities.
flavorText: "Burn it all and begin again," Letani Ospha urged, and from the ashes the old forests rose anew.
automationNotes: The target can accept: all their units leave the board, their home system is cleared, starting units are placed, they draw 2 action cards and replenish. Check the result on the map.

name: Ultimate Trickshot
window: When a player uses SUSTAIN DAMAGE in the active system, if that system is more than 5 hexes away from your home system and does not contain your units
text: Destroy that unit.
flavorText: From four systems away, a lone gunship took the shot. The dreadnought's shields had been holding. Then they weren't.
automationNotes: Listed under Check Combat Action Cards. The window also opens outside combat, for example against space cannon hits during movement; play it from your hand then. Destroy the unit yourself.

name: Ultimate Trickshot
window: When a player uses SUSTAIN DAMAGE in the active system, if that system is more than 5 hexes away from your home system and does not contain your units
text: Destroy that unit.
flavorText: The Mentak gunner never confirmed the kill. She was already pouring the drinks before the debris finished drifting.
automationNotes: Listed under Check Combat Action Cards. The window also opens outside combat, for example against space cannon hits during movement; play it from your hand then. Destroy the unit yourself.

name: Cumulative Support
text: Place infantry on a planet containing no other player's units equal to its distance from your home system, up to a maximum distance of 4.
flavorText: Every world the Sol fleet passed added a few more volunteers. By the end of the journey, they were an army.

name: Reality Disruption
window: After you activate a system in the Fracture that contains no planets and no other players' ships
text: You may treat this system as adjacent to all wormholes.
flavorText: Inside the Fracture, the Creuss navigators stopped trusting their instruments and started trusting their instincts. Space folded accordingly.
automationNotes: Not automated. The bot does not model the wormhole adjacency; move as if adjacent yourself.

name: Reality Disruption
window: After you activate a system in the Fracture that contains no planets and no other players' ships
text: You may treat this system as adjacent to all wormholes.
flavorText: The Ghosts of Creuss laughed at maps. In the Fracture, every wormhole was only a thought away.
automationNotes: Not automated. The bot does not model the wormhole adjacency; move as if adjacent yourself.

name: Corrupt Manifestation
text: Spend 2 influence to place 2 neutral infantry on 1 planet in the Fracture. If that planet contains another player's units, the neutral infantry resolve an invasion and ground combat against them.
flavorText: Something stirred on the Fracture's broken worlds: shapes that wore the faces of soldiers, marching under no banner at all.
automationNotes: Pay 2 influence with the payment buttons, then pick a Fracture planet for 2 neutral infantry. If players have ground forces there, the bot starts the ground combat against the planet's controller first; fight any other player there afterwards with /combat start_combat. If only structures are there, resolve the invasion by hand.

name: Creation of Glory
text: Reveal the top card of the relic deck. You may spend 5 resources to gain that relic. Otherwise, place it on the bottom of the relic deck.
notes: You gain exactly the revealed relic; abilities that change how you draw relics do not apply.
flavorText: The Titans of Ul raised a monument to their own legend, and in its foundations unearthed something older still.
automationNotes: Pay with the payment buttons; the bot does not check the amount.

name: Prophetic Declaration
text: Reveal the top card of the relic deck. You may spend 5 influence to gain that relic. Otherwise, place it on the bottom of the relic deck.
notes: You gain exactly the revealed relic; abilities that change how you draw relics do not apply.
flavorText: "It was foretold," the Yin Brotherhood proclaimed as their acolytes carried the relic from the vault. Few dared ask who had written the prophecy.
automationNotes: Pay with the payment buttons; the bot does not check the amount.

name: Resource Condensation
text: Reveal the top card of the relic deck. You may remove 2 command tokens from your command sheet to gain that relic. Otherwise, place it on the bottom of the relic deck.
notes: You gain exactly the revealed relic; abilities that change how you draw relics do not apply.
flavorText: The L1Z1X recalled two entire battle groups to fund the excavation. The Harrow's arithmetic, as always, was flawless.
automationNotes: The relic is gained first; then remove the 2 command tokens with the buttons.
